# Charge protected spectrum staging buffers to host and ingress budgets

Depends on #822, #826, #827 and #828 PASS/upstream. #825 is administratively stopped and superseded; its native baseline remains in the protected browser EQ branch. A fresh Astra XHIGH mainline integration review returned NO-GO before PR: public protected boot allocates two fixed 1,048,576-byte spectrum buffers after the resource projection, yet the protected projection passes spectrum_request=None and reports no FFI capture buffers. On the pinned shipped Wasm, host-only, ingress-only and combined 2,097,152-byte limits all incorrectly accepted a live protected handle. This issue owns one smallest closable product correction: budget the two fixed 1,048,576-byte payloads once in the host bridge report and protected ingress retained bound, refuse under-budget boot before those allocations/publication, reject allocator surplus capacity before installing either buffer, and qualify the rebuilt artifact. Browser receiver/SDK behavior, app adoption, generic budget tooling and one-shot delivery are separate work.

## Frozen decisions and scope

Keep Legacy spectrum-configured accounting, metadata/history charges and allocation timing unchanged. Protected boot receives a protected-only fixed-buffer payload charge; do not redefine spectrum_configured as spectrum_request-or-protected, because that would also charge unrelated Legacy metadata/history terms. Factor a checked two-buffer payload helper from the current FFI constant and reuse it in the existing Legacy buffer calculation without changing its value. Rust's `Vec::try_reserve_exact` guarantees capacity at least the requested size, not exactly that size: after each fallible reserve, reject any capacity above 1,048,576 with typed RefusedBudget before either buffer is installed. Drop temporary buffers and preserve committed endpoint output on that rejection. This explicitly permits a conforming overallocating allocator to refuse configuration; it cannot silently admit unbudgeted retained capacity. The protected charge adds exactly 2,097,152 bytes of installed buffer payload to bridge metadata/retained totals and a 1,048,576-byte buffer to largest-allocation maxima using max(previous, buffer payload). This retained-payload contract does not promise a preparation peak-memory or allocator-overhead ceiling. It is independent of spectrum-request capture maximum, ingress result limit and emitted payload length.

Apply the protected charge in hosts/host-web/src/lib.rs before retained_projection and before FFI prewarm. The corrected bridge report already feeds hosts/host-web/src/observation_ingress.rs; leave its additive_staging_bytes at zero for this charge, preserve its controller subtraction/private-target addition, and never count prepared graph/native storage again. Host-only refusal diagnostic is host.budget.retained_projection; ingress-only is web.observation.ingress.maximum_retained_bytes; with both low, host projection wins. Failed protected boot may have parsed/prepared off-render state but must not enter the fixed spectrum reserve branch, publish a live handle or erase previously committed endpoint output. Render code, ABI bytes and numeric identities do not change.

Allowed changes only: hosts/host-web/src/ffi.rs for fixed-capacity helper, test-only cold allocation-entry witness and focused public-boot fixtures; hosts/host-web/src/lib.rs for protected-only checked projection; hosts/host-web/src/tests.rs for coupled protected resource assertions; sdk/test/boot-evals.mjs for an extension of its existing actual-artifact protected boot test; hosts/host-web/web/miso-engine-v1-audio-worklet-artifact.sha256 for normal source-derived repin; this spec for decisions/evidence. No new crate, allocation framework, benchmark runner, SDK production reader, generator, build script, workflow or app edit. Newly necessary paths require rebrief before implementation.

## Objective discriminating gates

From two requested and installed buffer payloads of 1,048,576 bytes each, derive the independent literal 2,097,152-byte minimum floor. Check actual Vec capacities are exactly 1,048,576 only after successful production validation, not as an allocator assumption. Exercise surplus-capacity rejection with an explicitly oversized test Vec, without replacing the allocator; distinguish allocation/capacity refusal from a generous valid-budget success. Do not derive the refusal threshold from project_buffers, a resource report or an accepted boot. Use the existing valid one-track 48 kHz/128 protected preparation and generous 67,108,864-byte counterpart limits. Test host-only (2,097,152 host / 67,108,864 ingress), ingress-only (67,108,864 host / 2,097,152 ingress) and both-low (2,097,152 each). Each must refuse with handle zero and RefusedBudget, with the exact diagnostic above; an old-artifact run must execute all three even when an unexpected handle succeeds, release it, and collect the failures instead of aborting after the first.

On native, a separate cfg(test) thread-local counter increments only after configure_capture's already-configured early return and before either reserve; keep the counter outside counted staging layouts and production. Start each refusal from cold staging, require zero entries for each, one for valid configuration and no new entry on repeat configuration. Seed nondefault endpoint-output sentinels and require they survive refusal, with no live owner. Post-failure empty buffers alone do not prove no allocation because cleanup releases them. Two valid capture-request maxima must retain the same fixed buffer lengths/capacities. Existing inclusive/exact-fit fixtures supplement this independently derived floor.

Assert the exact equation `protected bridge = Legacy-unconfigured bridge - controller bytes + private target bytes + 2,097,152` independently for metadata and retained totals; largest-allocation fields equal max(the previous actual maxima, 1,048,576). Assert protected ingress retained calculation receives this corrected bridge increase exactly once, plus native reserved storage, with the controller/target adjustments applied once and additive_staging_bytes=0. Preserve Legacy configured and unconfigured report formulas. Native pointers may truncate above u32; use direct staging access for capacity evidence and the actual Wasm module for exported pointer evidence.

Extend the existing top-level protected observation shipped Wasm ABI and boot test without duplicating its setup or adding a runner. Preserve original JS-owned document bytes. Before each boot attempt restore the complete boot options (dispose of an unexpectedly successful handle resets all options), set the intended ingress limit, call document_ptr, copy the original JS-owned document again, and reacquire DataViews after allocation-capable calls: record_failure replaces staged document with diagnostics and invalidates it. Capture the exact diagnostic before restaging, execute all three low-limit cases and aggregate their outcomes after cleanup and generous recovery. Restore generous limits and the final successful protected boot; dispose unexpected handles, protect the intended assertion from cleanup failures, and verify the existing owner/pointers after the generous boot. Require the named actual-artifact filter to fail against preserved old Wasm for the three budget cases and pass against the rebuilt pinned Wasm.

Locked native host-web check, focused and full test-support library tests, strict all-targets/all-features Clippy, scalar wasm32 check with -simd128, simd128 check/build, SDK generated/type gates, realtime policy/mutation and shipped render-callgraph/resource gates, workspace format and diff are mandatory. Use CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/bl/misofm/engine/target for direct Cargo commands and pinned Rust 1.97.1. The normal builder uses its own fresh temporary target and remapped paths. Run repin mode once, record the source-derived SHA-256 and update only the pin, then run a second normal clean build into an existing empty directory. Repin mode prints the hash and exits before the seven output files; both scripts/check-web-audioworklet.sh and scripts/check-sdk-headless.sh must pass against that same rebuilt seven-file directory. Do not benchmark, retry/tune descriptive numbers or weaken old gates.

## Serial bounded execution and recovery

A: fresh Luna MAX edits only ffi.rs: factor the fixed two-buffer payload helper; add production surplus-capacity rejection before installing buffers and test it with an explicitly oversized Vec; add a test-only cold allocation-entry witness and focused successful-capacity/idempotence fixture; prove unchanged Legacy helper totals. Root audits, commits and pushes that exact-path green checkpoint before B.

B: fresh Luna MAX edits only lib.rs and the coupled tests.rs protected resource assertion/fixture: apply checked protected-only projection charge, compare exact two-buffer delta and ingress propagation, and pass focused/full native tests, Clippy, format and diff. Root audits, commits and pushes before C.

C: fresh Luna MAX edits only ffi.rs: native public protected-boot host-only/ingress-only/both refusal and diagnostic fixtures with cold zero-entry witness, endpoint sentinel, no owner, valid recovery and capture-limit independence. Root commits/pushes before D.

D1a: fresh Luna MAX edits only sdk/test/boot-evals.mjs: add a small complete-options/document restaging helper inside the existing protected artifact test, use it for the original generous boot, and keep the named old-artifact test green. Root commits/pushes this exact-path green checkpoint before D1b. D1b: a separate fresh Luna MAX edits only that test file: insert the three literal low-budget attempts using the helper, capture diagnostics/results before restaging, dispose unexpected handles, aggregate all outcomes after cleanup and generous recovery, and require old artifact red. Root commits a candid, buildable exact-path red checkpoint with evidence before any repin. If either slice cannot remain buildable/useful, reduce it rather than layering uncommitted work.

D2: root mechanically derives the new source hash through the normal builder, changes only the artifact pin, builds a second time to an existing empty output directory, and runs the frozen artifact/headless gates. Root commits/pushes the exact pin and complete evidence; no SDK fixture or production revision is hidden in this mechanical tranche.

One uncommitted implementation tranche at a time. Every coherent compiling/focused-green checkpoint pauses for root commit/status/upstream audit; a documented D1 red checkpoint is the sole planned exception. Do not carry a coherent tranche across three handoffs or 30 active minutes. Push checkpoint/evidence in the current checkpoint-push mode and synchronize this body with GitHub after material status changes.

At most four issue-wide candidate rounds: Luna MAX round 1, fresh Luna MAX round 2 if the first independent adversarial verdict fails, Sol HIGH round 3 if Luna cannot satisfy the bounded contract in two rounds, and Astra XHIGH round 4 if Sol cannot in one. Every candidate receives one fresh independent Astra MEDIUM issue-wide adversarial verdict; tranche labels and fixture-only revisions do not reset rounds. After round four FAIL, stop with preserved evidence and rebrief; no fifth retry or weakened gate. A fresh Astra XHIGH scoped this correction and directly reproduced all three old-artifact reds. A separate fresh Astra MEDIUM adversarial plan review returned NO-GO as first written; its amended brief included D split, diagnostics, restaging, cold witness, exact accounting and ledger. The corrected recheck returned NO-GO on the Rust Vec capacity assumption, the controller/target report equation, and complete options restoration after disposal; these are now amended. A second fresh independent Astra MEDIUM recheck at 44dccbb3 returned corrected PLAN GO with no blockers: both temporary Vec capacities can be validated before installation, host and ingress refusal precede prewarm, the explicit bridge equation applies adjustments once, and complete JS restaging exposes all old-artifact cases. Implementation may now start from this synchronized brief.
